newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North says Q1 iron ore output falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North says Q1 iron ore output falls.

text.p: Mining and forestry group North Ltd said on Friday that its share of iron ore production from the Robe River mine in Western Australia fell to 4.5 million tonnes in the September quarter from 5.0 million a year earlier.
"A planned five day engineering shutdown of the plant at Cape Lambert for extended plant maintenance following Cyclone Olivia contributed to the production fall," North said.
The company holds a 65 percent stake in Robe River.
"Global iron ore demand remained mixed in the major market regions with signs of strengthening in Japan offset by continued weakness in Europe, particularly in Germany," North said.
Energy Resources of Australia Ltd, 68.4 percent owned by North, reported uranium oxide production of 1,043 tonnes compared with 1,048 tonnes a year earlier.

North's 80 percent share of gold/copper production at the Northparkes mine in New South Wales was 13,732 tonnes of sulphide copper-gold concentrate and 3,636 tonnes of oxide copper-gold concentrate containing a combined 6,471 tonnes of copper and 15,429 ounces of gold.
The project was in start-up phase in the previous corresponding quarter.
North's 50 percent share of gold production at Kanowna Belle, near Kalgoorlie, Western Australia, totalled 19,965 ounces in the quarter, down from 22,847 a year earlier.
The decease in production resulted from lower mill head grades due to blending of grade material from stockpiles. Processing of this material will be completed in the December quarter, North said.
North's share of gold output from the Peak Hill mine in Western Australia was 6,908 ounces, little changed from the 6,903 ounces produced a year earlier.

Production of zinc at the Zincgruvan zinc, lead and silver mine in Sweden was 22,413 tonnes of zinc concentrate and 3,462 tonnes of lead concentrate from a total of 134,338 tonnes of ore treated. North took ownership of the mine earlier this year.
"Zinc grades continued to improve in the quarter, reaching 10 percent in September," North said.
In forest products, hardwood chips production fell to 452,395 tonnes in the quarter from 538,745 tonnes in the September quarter of 1995.
"Demand fell as customers moved to alternative suppliers due to earlier uncertainty over export licences," North said.
"Lower production was in line with reduced demand," it said.
The company said production in the forestry division was also hampered in the quarter by wet weather throughout Tasmania.
Production of softwood sawlogs totalled 27,442 tonnes, down from 33,508 tonnes in the previous corresponding quarter.
Production of softwood pulplogs and chips totalled 23,587 tonnes, down from 97,417.
"Both domestic and export softwood markets remained depressed throughout the quarter," North said.
"In addition, export log customers reduced order intakes to lower inventories, as the market remained weak," it said.
